unit.why: A short exemplum cited from Sefer Hasidim (via Shem mi-Shimon, Be-ha'alotkha) about a villager-shamash whose devekut while lighting the lamps is noticed by the town rabbi; it is a pre-Hasidic tale, not a Hasidic one.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a thematic chain on lighting lamps; the previous division ends with the heading 'מענין הדלקת נרות' and the next continues with homiletic material from Dudaim ba-Sadeh.

stories.end_quote: ומיד נתן לו נשיאותו וכו׳ עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: A villager who became beadle of the study hall was so absorbed in cleaving to God while lighting the lamps that he poured the oil on his feet; the town rabbi noticed this, declared him fit to be rabbi and handed him his leadership.

tags.why: Praise of a pious man, taken explicitly from Sefer Hasidim.

quotes: מרוב דבקותו בהש״י לא היה מרגיש מה הוא עושה
tags.why: Rapt attachment to God shown during his task.
The story's central experience is mystical cleaving.
He serves as beadle of the study hall, where the lamps are lit.

quotes: בבן כפר שהלך לדור בעיר ונעשה שמש
tags.why: A humble beadle whose hidden piety is concealed.
The beadle's hidden greatness is disclosed to the rabbi and he is elevated.

quotes: אמר תמה אני כי מהראוי הוא שיהא רב
tags.why: The rabbi realizes the lowly beadle is worthy of leadership.
The rabbi hands his leadership over to the beadle.
A pious man in a lowly role, implicitly a model of humility.
